name: continuous_update_slot
doc: **Varying one slot of a point sequence is continuous.** The outer step of the path.
stmt:
theorem continuous_update_slot (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (a : ℕ) :
    Continuous (fun v : Pt n => Function.update pts a v)
proof: Continuous.update continuous_const a continuous_id

name: continuous_samePoint_path
doc: **The `.samePoint` path is continuous.**
stmt:
theorem continuous_samePoint_path (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (a : ℕ) (i : Fin n) :
    Continuous (fun t : ℝ =>
      Function.update pts a (Function.update (pts a) i (pts a i + t)))
proof:
by
  have h1 : Continuous (fun t : ℝ => Function.update (pts a) i (pts a i + t)) :=
    continuous_update_coord (pts a) i
  exact Continuous.update continuous_const a h1

name: samePoint_path_zero
doc: **The path starts at `pts`.**
stmt:
theorem samePoint_path_zero (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (a : ℕ) (i : Fin n) :
    Function.update pts a (Function.update (pts a) i (pts a i + 0)) = pts
proof:
by
  simp

name: samePoint_path_of_ne
doc: **The path leaves every other slot alone.**
stmt:
theorem samePoint_path_of_ne (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (a : ℕ) (i : Fin n) (t : ℝ) {j : ℕ} (hj : j ≠ a) :
    Function.update pts a (Function.update (pts a) i (pts a i + t)) j = pts j
proof: Function.update_noteq hj _ pts

name: sq_lt_sq_iff_mul_sign
doc: **Squaring loses a comparison exactly when the sign condition holds.**
stmt:
theorem sq_lt_sq_iff_mul_sign (d t : ℝ) :
    (d + t) ^ 2 < d ^ 2 ↔ t * (2 * d + t) < 0
proof:
by
  constructor
  · intro h; nlinarith
  · intro h; nlinarith

name: sqDist_along_path_split
doc: **The penalty along the path, with the moving coordinate split off.**
stmt:
theorem sqDist_along_path_split (p q : Pt n) (i : Fin n) (t : ℝ) :
    sqDist (n := n) (Function.update p i (p i + t)) q
      = (p i + t - q i) ^ 2 + ∑ j in Finset.univ \ {i}, (p j - q j) ^ 2
proof:
by
  rw [sqDist_eq_coord_add_rest]
  congr 1
  · rw [Function.update_same]
  · refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun j hj => ?_)
    have hji : j ≠ i := by
      intro h
      exact (Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hj).2 (by simp [h])
    rw [Function.update_noteq hji]

name: sqDist_along_path_lt
doc:
**Along the path the penalty strictly decreases**, provided the sign condition on `t` holds.

The hypothesis keeps two questions apart: whether a decreasing `t` exists is arithmetic
(`sq_lt_sq_iff_mul_sign`), whether it is small enough to stay inside a neighbourhood is topology.
proof:
by
  rw [sqDist_along_path_split, sqDist_eq_coord_add_rest]
  have hsq := (sq_lt_sq_iff_mul_sign (p i - q i) t).mpr h
  linarith

name: neg_mul_two_add_neg_mul_neg
doc:
**The sign condition holds for a scaled `-d`.** With `0 < m <= 1`, the point `-d * m` lies in the interval where
the product is negative.
stmt:
theorem neg_mul_two_add_neg_mul_neg (d m : ℝ) (hd : d ≠ 0) (hm0 : 0 < m) (hm1 : m ≤ 1) :
    -d * m * (2 * d + -d * m) < 0
proof:
by
  have hd2 : 0 < d ^ 2 := by positivity
  have hpos : 0 < m * (2 - m) := by nlinarith
  have hEq : -d * m * (2 * d + -d * m) = -(d ^ 2) * m * (2 - m) := by ring
  rw [hEq]
  nlinarith

name: exists_small_descent
doc:
**A decreasing step can be made arbitrarily small.**

For every `ε > 0` there is a `t` with `0 < |t| < ε` satisfying the sign condition of `sqDist_along_path_lt`. This is
the arithmetic half of "the path leaves the point in a decreasing direction *and* stays nearby"; the topology is in
`continuous_samePoint_path`.
stmt:
theorem exists_small_descent (d : ℝ) (hd : d ≠ 0) {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∃ t : ℝ, t ≠ 0 ∧ |t| < ε ∧ t * (2 * d + t) < 0
proof:
by
  have hDpos : 0 < |d| := abs_pos.mpr hd
  set m : ℝ := min 1 (ε / (2 * |d|)) with hm
  have hmpos : 0 < m := by
    rw [hm]
    exact lt_min one_pos (by positivity)
  have hm1 : m ≤ 1 := by rw [hm]; exact min_le_left _ _
  have hmle : m ≤ ε / (2 * |d|) := by rw [hm]; exact min_le_right _ _
  have hm0 : 0 ≤ m := le_of_lt hmpos
  refine ⟨-d * m, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  ·                        
    intro hzero
    have hdm : d * m = 0 := by linarith
    rcases mul_eq_zero.mp hdm with h | h
    · exact hd h
    · exact (ne_of_gt hmpos) h
  ·                     
    have hDm : |d| * m ≤ ε / 2 := by
      calc |d| * m ≤ |d| * (ε / (2 * |d|)) :=
              mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hmle (le_of_lt hDpos)
        _ = ε / 2 := by field_simp; ring
    have habs : |-d * m| = |d| * m := by
      rw [abs_mul, abs_neg, abs_of_pos hmpos]
    rw [habs]
    linarith
  ·                            
    have := neg_mul_two_add_neg_mul_neg d m hd hmpos hm1
    linarith [this]

name: not_eventually_zero_of_small_counterexample
doc:
**An `Eventually` property at `0` is incompatible with counterexamples at every scale.**

The general form of the last step. Note the hypothesis is exactly what `exists_small_descent` provides: for every
`ε > 0`, a `t` with `|t| < ε` where the property fails.
stmt:
theorem not_eventually_zero_of_small_counterexample {P : ℝ → Prop}
    (h : ∀ᶠ t in nhds (0 : ℝ), P t)
    (hbad : ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∃ t : ℝ, |t| < ε ∧ ¬ P t) :
    False
proof:
by
  obtain ⟨d, hd, hdprop⟩ := Metric.eventually_nhds_iff.mp h
  obtain ⟨t, ht, hnot⟩ := hbad d hd
  exact hnot (hdprop (by simpa [Real.dist_eq, sub_zero] using ht))

name: sqDist_samePoint_not_localMin
doc:
**A configuration with `pts a ≠ pts b` is not a local minimum of the `.samePoint` penalty's square.**

The five earlier pieces feed this: local minimality pulls back along `continuous_samePoint_path` to an `Eventually`
statement at `0`, `exists_small_descent` supplies a witness at every scale, and
`not_eventually_zero_of_small_counterexample` turns the pair into a contradiction.

Nothing here is specific to `EqConstraint.poly (.samePoint a b)` beyond reading its penalty as `sqDist (pts a) (pts b)`.
stmt:
theorem sqDist_samePoint_not_localMin (a b : ℕ) (ha : a ≠ b) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (hne : pts a ≠ pts b) :
    ¬ IsLocalMin (fun x : ℕ → Pt n => (sqDist (n := n) (x a) (x b)) ^ 2) pts
proof:
by
  intro hmin
                            
  have hex : ∃ i : Fin n, pts a i ≠ pts b i := by
    by_contra hall
    push_neg at hall
    exact hne (funext hall)
  obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := hex
  have hd : pts a i - pts b i ≠ 0 := sub_ne_zero.mpr hi
                                                  
  have hcont : Filter.Tendsto
      (fun t : ℝ => Function.update pts a (Function.update (pts a) i (pts a i + t)))
      (nhds (0 : ℝ)) (nhds pts) := by
    have hc := (continuous_samePoint_path pts a i).tendsto 0
    simpa using hc
                                              
  have hev : ∀ᶠ t in nhds (0 : ℝ),
      (sqDist (n := n) (pts a) (pts b)) ^ 2
        ≤ (sqDist (n := n)
            ((fun s : ℝ => Function.update pts a (Function.update (pts a) i (pts a i + s))) t a)
            ((fun s : ℝ => Function.update pts a (Function.update (pts a) i (pts a i + s))) t b)) ^ 2 :=
    hcont.eventually hmin
                                      
  refine not_eventually_zero_of_small_counterexample hev (fun ε hε => ?_)
  obtain ⟨t, _ht0, htε, htlt⟩ := exists_small_descent (pts a i - pts b i) hd hε
  refine ⟨t, htε, ?_⟩
                                                           
  set A : ℝ := sqDist (n := n) (Function.update (pts a) i (pts a i + t)) (pts b) with hA
  set B : ℝ := sqDist (n := n) (pts a) (pts b) with hB
  have hnnA : (0 : ℝ) ≤ A := by rw [hA]; exact sqDist_nonneg _ _
  have hlt : A < B := by
    rw [hA, hB]
    exact sqDist_along_path_lt (pts a) (pts b) i htlt

name: sqDist_eq_resid
doc:
**`sqDist` on the flattened carrier is `Differentiable`'s residual.**

The two files reach the same function by different routes: `Dist` defines `sqDist` as a sum over coordinates of
squared differences of `Pt` components, and `Differentiable` builds `∑ i, segComp a b i v ^ 2` from projections.
This lemma is where they are identified, and it is what lets the smoothness result transfer.
stmt:
theorem sqDist_eq_resid {k : ℕ} (a b : Fin k) (v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) :
    sqDist (n := n) (unflatten v a) (unflatten v b)
      = ∑ i, segComp a b i v ^ 2
proof:
by
  unfold sqDist segComp Lattice.Lib.Linear.PenaltyVector.sqNorm diff
  refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_)
  ring

name: differentiable_sqDist
doc: **The squared distance between two points is differentiable on the flattened carrier.**
stmt:
theorem differentiable_sqDist {k : ℕ} (a b : Fin k) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ =>
      sqDist (n := n) (unflatten v a) (unflatten v b))
proof:
by
  simpa only [sqDist_eq_resid] using differentiable_sqDistResid (n := n) a b

name: differentiable_sqDistEqPenalty
doc:
**`sqDistEq`'s penalty is differentiable**, whenever the expression on the right side is.

The hypothesis `hd` is the expression's smoothness, which `Lattice.Geo.ExprDeriv.hasFDerivAt_eval` supplies for any
`GeoExpr` on a large enough carrier. Stating it as a hypothesis keeps this file independent of the carrier bound.
stmt:
theorem differentiable_sqDistEqPenalty {k : ℕ} (a b : Fin k) (d : GeoExpr n)
    (hd : Differentiable ℝ (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => d.evalPts (toNatConfig v))) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => sqDistEqPenalty a b d (toNatConfig v))
proof:
by
                                                                                   
  have h : (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => sqDistEqPenalty a b d (toNatConfig v))
      = fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ =>
          (sqDist (n := n) (unflatten v a) (unflatten v b) - d.evalPts (toNatConfig v)) ^ 2 := by
    funext v
    unfold sqDistEqPenalty twoValuedPenalty
                                                                   
    have hc : ∀ i : Fin k, toNatConfig v i = unflatten v i := by
      intro i
      unfold toNatConfig
      rw [dif_pos i.isLt]
    simp only [hc]
  rw [h]
  exact ((differentiable_sqDist a b).sub hd).pow 2

name: differentiable_equalLengthPenalty
doc: **`equalLength`'s penalty is differentiable**: a difference of two squared distances, squared.
stmt:
theorem differentiable_equalLengthPenalty {k : ℕ} (a b c e : Fin k) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => equalLengthPenalty a b c e (toNatConfig v))
proof:
by
  have h : (fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ => equalLengthPenalty a b c e (toNatConfig v))
      = fun v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ =>
          (sqDist (n := n) (unflatten v a) (unflatten v b)
            - sqDist (n := n) (unflatten v c) (unflatten v e)) ^ 2 := by
    funext v
    unfold equalLengthPenalty twoValuedPenalty
    have hc : ∀ i : Fin k, toNatConfig v i = unflatten v i := by
      intro i
      unfold toNatConfig
      rw [dif_pos i.isLt]
    simp only [hc]
  rw [h]
  exact ((differentiable_sqDist a b).sub (differentiable_sqDist c e)).pow 2

end Lattice.Geo

name: bump_self
stmt:
@[simp] theorem bump_self (b : Fin k) (i : Fin n) :
    bump k n b i (flatEquiv k n (b, i)) = 1
proof:
by
  simp [bump]

name: bump_ne
stmt:
theorem bump_ne {b : Fin k} {i : Fin n} {j : Fin (k * n)}
    (h : j ≠ flatEquiv k n (b, i)) : bump k n b i j = 0
proof:
by
  simp [bump, h]

name: unflatten_add
doc: **`unflatten` is additive**: it reads one entry, and reading is additive.
stmt:
theorem unflatten_add (v w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ) (p : Fin k) (q : Fin n) :
    unflatten (v + w) p q = unflatten v p q + unflatten w p q
proof:
by
  simp [unflatten]

name: unflatten_smul_bump_same
doc:
**Reading the bumped entry gives the scale.** Here `flatEquiv`'s injectivity is used: equal images
force the pairs to be equal.
stmt:
theorem unflatten_smul_bump_same (b : Fin k) (i : Fin n) (t : ℝ) :
    unflatten (t • bump k n b i) b i = t
proof:
by
  simp [unflatten, bump]

name: unflatten_smul_bump_ne
doc: **Reading any other entry of a bumped vector gives zero.**
stmt:
theorem unflatten_smul_bump_ne {b p : Fin k} {i q : Fin n} (hpq : ¬(p = b ∧ q = i)) (t : ℝ) :
    unflatten (t • bump k n b i) p q = 0
proof:
by
  simp only [unflatten, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
  have hne : flatEquiv k n (p, q) ≠ flatEquiv k n (b, i) := by
    intro h
    exact hpq (Prod.ext_iff.mp (Equiv.injective _ h))
  rw [bump_ne hne, mul_zero]

name: unflatten_add_smul_bump
doc: **How `unflatten` responds to a bump**, in the single form the geometry cites.
stmt:
theorem unflatten_add_smul_bump (b : Fin k) (i : Fin n) (t : ℝ) (v : Fin (k * n) → ℝ)
    (p : Fin k) (q : Fin n) :
    unflatten (v + t • bump k n b i) p q
      = unflatten v p q + (if p = b ∧ q = i then t else 0)
proof:
by
  by_cases h : p = b ∧ q = i
  · rw [if_pos h]
    obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := h
    rw [unflatten_add, unflatten_smul_bump_same]
  · rw [if_neg h, unflatten_add, unflatten_smul_bump_ne h, add_zero]

name: ofLinearFormAux_eval
doc: **The embedding evaluates to the form's value at point `0`**, for any index list.
stmt:
theorem ofLinearFormAux_eval (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (l : List (Fin n))
    (hl : l.Nodup) :
    (ofLinearFormAux c l).evalPts pts
      = c.b + (l.map (fun i => c.a i * pts 0 i)).sum
proof:
by
  induction l with
  | nil =>
    show c.b = c.b + ([] : List ℝ).sum
    simp
  | cons i rest ih =>
    have hrest : rest.Nodup := (List.nodup_cons.mp hl).2
                                                       
    show (linTerm c i).evalPts pts + (ofLinearFormAux c rest).evalPts pts
      = c.b + (c.a i * pts 0 i + (rest.map (fun j => c.a j * pts 0 j)).sum)
    rw [ih hrest]
    have hterm : (linTerm c i).evalPts pts = c.a i * pts 0 i := by
      unfold linTerm
      show c.a i * pts 0 i = c.a i * pts 0 i
      rfl
    rw [hterm]
    ring

name: ofLinearForm_evalPts
doc: **The embedding evaluates to the form's value at point `0`.**
stmt:
theorem ofLinearForm_evalPts (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (ofLinearForm c).evalPts pts
      = c.b + ∑ i : Fin n, c.a i * pts 0 i
proof:
by
  rw [ofLinearForm, ofLinearFormAux_eval c pts (List.finRange n) (List.nodup_finRange n)]
  congr 1

name: holds_ofLinearForm_iff
doc:
**The embedded constraint is satisfied exactly where the form vanishes.**

The symbolic half of the chain: `ofLinearForm` turns the decoded form into a `GeoConstraint`, and its
satisfaction is the form's vanishing.
stmt:
theorem holds_ofLinearForm_iff (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.eqZero (ofLinearForm c)) pts ↔ (ofLinearForm c).evalPts pts = 0
proof: Iff.rfl

name: token_to_weight
doc:
**The four-hop chain, stated in one theorem.**

A linear form `c` -- obtained from a token stream by `Lattice.Lift.decodePayload`, whose success is the
hypothesis `hdec` -- compiles to a geometric constraint whose satisfaction is `c`'s vanishing, with the value
computed at point `0`.

This is the first statement in the project that uses **both** ends: the token layer's `encodeForm` and
`decodePayload` from `Lattice.Lift.L1L2`, and `GeoConstraint` from `Lattice.Geo`.

The decode is carried as a hypothesis rather than proved because `decodePayload` returns an `Option`:
`Lattice.Lift.L1L2.arity_is_load_bearing` shows the arity is recoverable, not that every stream is a valid
encoding. What the statement does **not** claim: that the decode is total, or that `ofLinearForm` is
injective. It says the chain preserves meaning where it applies.
stmt:
theorem token_to_weight (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (rs : List ℝ)
    (_hdec : Lattice.Lift.decodePayload n rs = some c) :
    (GeoConstraint.Holds (.eqZero (ofLinearForm c)) pts ↔ (ofLinearForm c).evalPts pts = 0) ∧
      (ofLinearForm c).evalPts pts = c.b + ∑ i : Fin n, c.a i * pts 0 i
proof: ⟨holds_ofLinearForm_iff c pts, ofLinearForm_evalPts c pts⟩

name: lossOfLinearForm_eq_zero
doc:
**The penalty vanishes exactly where the linear form does.**

The last hop of the chain, and the point at which the result is about a **weight-side quantity** rather than a
predicate: `lossOfLinearForm c pts = 0` is the equation a training loop would drive down, and this says its
zero set is the form's vanishing set.

Composed from `Lattice.Geo.Loss.loss_eq_zero_expr` (the penalty of an `expr` constraint is zero iff the
expression is) and `ofLinearForm_evalPts` (the embedding computes the form's value).
stmt:
theorem lossOfLinearForm_eq_zero (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    lossOfLinearForm c pts = 0 ↔ (ofLinearForm c).evalPts pts = 0
proof:
by
  unfold lossOfLinearForm eqOfLinearForm
  exact EqConstraint.loss_eq_zero_expr (ofLinearForm c) pts

name: token_to_loss
doc:
**The four-hop chain, reaching the weight side.**

A token stream that decodes to a linear form `c` yields a penalty whose zero set is exactly `c`'s vanishing
set, and whose value at any configuration is the square of the form's value at point `0`.

This is `token_to_weight` with the final hop added: the object on the right is a function
`(ℕ → Pt n) → ℝ`, which is what a training procedure consumes. The decode remains a hypothesis for the reason
given there.
stmt:
theorem token_to_loss (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (rs : List ℝ)
    (_hdec : Lattice.Lift.decodePayload n rs = some c) :
    (lossOfLinearForm c pts = 0 ↔ (ofLinearForm c).evalPts pts = 0) ∧
      (ofLinearForm c).evalPts pts = c.b + ∑ i : Fin n, c.a i * pts 0 i
proof: ⟨lossOfLinearForm_eq_zero c pts, ofLinearForm_evalPts c pts⟩

name: lossOfLinearForm_nonneg
doc:
**The penalty is non-negative**, so driving it to zero is a well-posed objective rather than a search for a
sign change.
stmt:
theorem lossOfLinearForm_nonneg (c : Lattice.Core.LinearForm ℝ n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    0 ≤ lossOfLinearForm c pts
proof:
by
  unfold lossOfLinearForm eqOfLinearForm
  exact EqConstraint.loss_nonneg (.expr (ofLinearForm c)) pts

end Lattice.Geo

name: cofactor_eq_zero_of_plucker_zero
doc:
**A vanishing sum of squares has every summand zero**, in the two-index form used below.

Pulled out as its own lemma because the induction over two nested `Finset.sum`s is the mechanical part of the
argument and should not obscure the geometry.
stmt:
theorem cofactor_eq_zero_of_plucker_zero (u v : Pt n) (h : pluckerNorm u v = 0)
    (i j : Fin n) : cofactor u v i j = 0
proof:
by
  unfold pluckerNorm at h
                                                                                           
  have hnonneg : ∀ i ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n)),
      0 ≤ ∑ j : Fin n, (cofactor u v i j) ^ 2 := by
    intro i _
    exact Finset.sum_nonneg (fun j _ => sq_nonneg _)
  have hrow := (Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg hnonneg).mp h i (Finset.mem_univ i)
  exact pow_eq_zero_iff (n := 2) (by norm_num) |>.mp
    ((Finset.sum_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg (fun j _ => sq_nonneg _)).mp hrow j (Finset.mem_univ j))

name: poly_lipschitz_expr
doc: **`.expr` 分支**：就是表达式的 Lipschitz 性质。
stmt:
theorem poly_lipschitz_expr {n k : ℕ} (e : GeoExpr n) {K : ℝ}
    (h : LipschitzK n k e K) :
    ∀ pts pts' : ℕ → Pt n,
      |GeoExpr.evalPts e pts - GeoExpr.evalPts e pts'| ≤ K * rho n k pts pts'
proof: h

name: poly_lipschitz_samePoint
doc: **`.samePoint` 分支**：直接是 `sqDist_lipschitz`。
stmt:
theorem poly_lipschitz_samePoint {n k : ℕ} {pts pts' : ℕ → Pt n} {a b : ℕ} {B : ℝ}
    (ha : a < k) (hb : b < k) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    (hpts : ∀ p i, |pts p i| ≤ B) (hpts' : ∀ p i, |pts' p i| ≤ B) :
    |sqDist (n := n) (pts a) (pts b) - sqDist (n := n) (pts' a) (pts' b)|
      ≤ sqDistConst n B * rho n k pts pts'
proof: sqDist_lipschitz ha hb hB hpts hpts'

name: poly_lipschitz_distEq
doc: **`.distEq` 分支**：`sqDist` 减表达式，常数相加。
stmt:
theorem poly_lipschitz_distEq {n k : ℕ} {pts pts' : ℕ → Pt n} {a b : ℕ} {d : GeoExpr n}
    {B Kd : ℝ} (ha : a < k) (hb : b < k) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    (hpts : ∀ p i, |pts p i| ≤ B) (hpts' : ∀ p i, |pts' p i| ≤ B)
    (hd : |GeoExpr.evalPts d pts - GeoExpr.evalPts d pts'| ≤ Kd * rho n k pts pts') :
    |(sqDist (n := n) (pts a) (pts b) - GeoExpr.evalPts d pts)
        - (sqDist (n := n) (pts' a) (pts' b) - GeoExpr.evalPts d pts')|
      ≤ (sqDistConst n B + Kd) * rho n k pts pts'
proof:
by
  have hρ := rho_nonneg n k pts pts'
  have hsq := sqDist_lipschitz (n := n) (k := k) (pts := pts) (pts' := pts')
    (a := a) (b := b) ha hb hB hpts hpts'
  have heq : (sqDist (n := n) (pts a) (pts b) - GeoExpr.evalPts d pts)
        - (sqDist (n := n) (pts' a) (pts' b) - GeoExpr.evalPts d pts')
      = (sqDist (n := n) (pts a) (pts b) - sqDist (n := n) (pts' a) (pts' b))
        - (GeoExpr.evalPts d pts - GeoExpr.evalPts d pts') := by ring
  rw [heq]
  calc |(sqDist (n := n) (pts a) (pts b) - sqDist (n := n) (pts' a) (pts' b))
          - (GeoExpr.evalPts d pts - GeoExpr.evalPts d pts')|
      ≤ |sqDist (n := n) (pts a) (pts b) - sqDist (n := n) (pts' a) (pts' b)|
          + |GeoExpr.evalPts d pts - GeoExpr.evalPts d pts'| := abs_sub _ _
    _ ≤ sqDistConst n B * rho n k pts pts' + Kd * rho n k pts pts' := by
        exact add_le_add hsq hd
    _ = (sqDistConst n B + Kd) * rho n k pts pts' := by ring

name: poly_lipschitz_perpendicular
doc: **`.perpendicular` 分支**：双线性求和，常数 `sqDistConst n B`。
stmt:
theorem poly_lipschitz_perpendicular {n k : ℕ} {pts pts' : ℕ → Pt n} {a b c e : ℕ} {B : ℝ}
    (ha : a < k) (hb : b < k) (hc : c < k) (he : e < k) (hB : 0 ≤ B)
    (hpts : ∀ p i, |pts p i| ≤ B) (hpts' : ∀ p i, |pts' p i| ≤ B) :
    |(∑ i : Fin n, (pts b i - pts a i) * (pts e i - pts c i))
        - (∑ i : Fin n, (pts' b i - pts' a i) * (pts' e i - pts' c i))|
      ≤ sqDistConst n B * rho n k pts pts'
proof:
bilinearSum_lipschitz ha hb hc he hB hpts hpts'

end Lattice.Geo

name: sqDistConst_scale
doc: **`sqDistConst` 对 `B` 是线性的。** 单位框的常数 `8n` 是基数。
stmt:
theorem sqDistConst_scale (n : ℕ) (B : ℝ) :
    sqDistConst n B = B * sqDistConst n 1
proof:
by
  unfold sqDistConst
  ring

name: sqDistConst_one
doc: 单位框下 `sqDist` 的常数是 `8n`。
stmt: theorem sqDistConst_one (n : ℕ) : sqDistConst n 1 = 8 * n
proof:
by
  unfold sqDistConst
  ring

                           

                                               
                                                                        

mutual

name: poly_const_samePoint
doc: **`samePoint`**：单位框下常数 `8n`。
stmt: theorem poly_const_samePoint (n : ℕ) : sqDistConst n 1 = 8 * n
proof: sqDistConst_one n

name: poly_const_perpendicular
doc:
**`perpendicular`**：与 `samePoint` 相同，也是 `8n`。
两者是同一个双线性型估计（见 `PolyLipschitz` 文件头）。
stmt: theorem poly_const_perpendicular (n : ℕ) : sqDistConst n 1 = 8 * n
proof: sqDistConst_one n

name: poly_const_distEq
doc: **`distEq`**：`8n + K_d`。
stmt:
theorem poly_const_distEq (n : ℕ) (Kd : ℝ) :
    sqDistConst n 1 + Kd = 8 * n + Kd
proof:
by
  rw [sqDistConst_one]

                               

                
example : sqDistConst 2 1 = 16 := by rw [sqDistConst_one]; norm_num
                
example : sqDistConst 3 1 = 24 := by rw [sqDistConst_one]; norm_num
                               
example : sqDistConst 3 2 = 48 := by unfold sqDistConst; norm_num

end Lattice.Geo

name: poly_expr_localMin_implies_zero
doc:
**The `.expr` branch is covered by the derivative argument.**

`EqConstraint.poly (.expr e) pts` is by definition `e.evalPts pts`, and `Lattice.Geo.ExprLocalMin` already bridges
`evalPts` to the local-minimum argument. The one thing this theorem adds is the change of variable: `ExprLocalMin`
phrases the statement over `Fin (k * n) → ℝ` through `toNatConfig`, so a caller holding a point sequence needs
`k` past `e.maxPoint` to read it back.

The hypothesis `hne` is `derivExpr k e w ≠ 0` -- the residual's derivative at the read-back configuration. It is
the honest hypothesis rather than a gap: a constant expression has zero derivative everywhere, and its penalty is
minimised at every point without vanishing (`Lattice.Geo.ExprLocalMin.constExpr_localMin_counterexample`).
stmt:
theorem poly_expr_localMin_implies_zero
    (e : GeoExpr n) (k : ℕ) (hk : e.maxPoint < k) (w : Fin (k * n) → ℝ)
    (hne : derivExpr k e w ≠ 0)
    (hmin : IsLocalMin (fun y : Fin (k * n) → ℝ =>
      (EqConstraint.poly (.expr e) (toNatConfig y)) ^ 2) w) :
    EqConstraint.poly (.expr e) (toNatConfig w) = 0
proof: evalPts_localMin_implies_zero k e hk w hne hmin

name: poly_samePoint_eq_sqDist
doc:
**The `.samePoint` branch's penalty is `sqDist`**, and therefore non-negative.

Recorded as its own statement because the branch is what makes the non-negativity route applicable, and because a
reader checking coverage should be able to see the reason at a glance.
stmt:
theorem poly_samePoint_eq_sqDist (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    EqConstraint.poly (.samePoint a b) pts = sqDist (n := n) (pts a) (pts b)
proof: rfl

name: poly_samePoint_nonneg
doc: **The `.samePoint` penalty is non-negative.**
stmt:
theorem poly_samePoint_nonneg (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    0 ≤ EqConstraint.poly (.samePoint a b) pts
proof:
by
  rw [poly_samePoint_eq_sqDist]
  exact sqDist_nonneg (n := n) (pts a) (pts b)

name: poly_samePoint_eq_zero_iff
doc: **The `.samePoint` penalty vanishes exactly on the coincident configurations.**
stmt:
theorem poly_samePoint_eq_zero_iff (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    EqConstraint.poly (.samePoint a b) pts = 0 ↔ pts a = pts b
proof:
by
  rw [poly_samePoint_eq_sqDist]
  exact sqDist_eq_zero_iff (n := n) (pts a) (pts b)

name: distEq_penalty_pos_of_neg_const
doc: **A negative constant makes the `.distEq` penalty strictly positive.**
stmt:
theorem distEq_penalty_pos_of_neg_const (p q : Pt n) {c : ℝ} (hc : c < 0) :
    0 < sqDist (n := n) p q - c
proof:
by
  have h := sqDist_nonneg (n := n) p q
  linarith

name: distEq_sq_penalty_ge_sq
doc:
**The squared `.distEq` penalty is bounded below by a strictly positive number.**

`0 <= sqDist` forces `-c <= sqDist - c`, and `c < 0` makes `c ^ 2` positive, so the square never comes near zero.
This is the substantive form of the counterexample: it says the infimum of the squared penalty is not `0`, hence a
local minimum of it cannot be a zero of the penalty.

An earlier attempt stated the same idea with a hypothesis `sqDist p q = 0`. That hypothesis is not free: by
`Lattice.Geo.Dist.sqDist_eq_zero_iff` it forces `p = q`, so the resulting equation said nothing about `c` at all. The
bound below avoids the vacuity by comparing against `c ^ 2` rather than against an attained value.
stmt:
theorem distEq_sq_penalty_ge_sq (p q : Pt n) {c : ℝ} (hc : c < 0) :
    c ^ 2 ≤ (sqDist (n := n) p q - c) ^ 2
proof:
by
  have h := sqDist_nonneg (n := n) p q
  have hc' : c ≤ sqDist (n := n) p q - c := by linarith
  nlinarith [sq_nonneg (sqDist (n := n) p q - c), hc']

name: neg_const_sq_pos
doc: **That lower bound is strictly positive.**
stmt: theorem neg_const_sq_pos {c : ℝ} (hc : c < 0) : 0 < c ^ 2
proof:
by
  nlinarith

end Lattice.Geo

name: const_one_unsatisfiable
doc:
**`eqZero (.const 1)` 对任何点配置都不成立。**

`1 ≠ 0`。⇒ 要求它的修复算子，等于要求一个不存在的解存在。
stmt:
theorem const_one_unsatisfiable (n : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    ¬ GeoConstraint.Holds (.eqZero (.const 1)) pts
proof:
by
  intro h
  simp only [GeoConstraint.Holds, GeoExpr.evalPts] at h
  norm_num at h

name: repair_of_satisfiable
doc:
**约束可满足 ⟹ 存在修复算子。**

构造：已满足的点不动，未满足的点一步跳到解 `x₀`；`μ` 取指示。
stmt:
theorem repair_of_satisfiable (Sat : α → Prop) (h : ∃ x, Sat x) :
    ∃ R : Repair α, ∀ x, R.Sat x ↔ Sat x
proof:
by
  classical
  obtain ⟨x₀, hx₀⟩ := h
  refine ⟨{
    Sat := Sat
    fix := fun x => if Sat x then x else x₀
    μ := fun x => if Sat x then 0 else 1
    absorbs := ?_
    decreases := ?_
    atomic := ?_
  }, fun x => Iff.rfl⟩
  · intro x hx
    simp only [hx, if_true]
  · intro x hx
    simp only [hx, if_false, hx₀, if_true]
    norm_num
  · intro x hx
    by_contra hnot
    simp only [hnot, if_false] at hx
    exact absurd hx (by norm_num)

name: satisfiable_of_repair
doc:
**存在修复算子 ⟹ 约束可满足。**

取 `μ` 的全局最小值点。若它不满足，`decreases` 给出更小的 `μ`，矛盾。
stmt:
theorem satisfiable_of_repair (R : Repair α) (hz : ∃ x, R.μ x = 0) :
    ∃ x, R.Sat x
proof:
by
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hz
  exact ⟨x, R.atomic x hx⟩

name: repair_iff_satisfiable
doc:
**中心结论：可修复 ⟺ 可满足。**

对**任意** `Sat : α → Prop` 成立，因此四个多项式形式
（`eqZero`、`leZero`、`ltZero`、`gtZero`）共用这一条。
stmt:
theorem repair_iff_satisfiable (Sat : α → Prop) :
    (∃ R : Repair α, (∀ x, R.Sat x ↔ Sat x) ∧ ∃ x, R.μ x = 0) ↔ (∃ x, Sat x)
proof:
by
  classical
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨R, hR, hz⟩
    obtain ⟨x, hsat⟩ := satisfiable_of_repair R hz
    exact ⟨x, (hR x).mp hsat⟩
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨s, hs⟩ := h
                                                                                          
    refine ⟨{
      Sat := Sat
      fix := fun x => if Sat x then x else s
      μ := fun x => if Sat x then 0 else 1
      absorbs := ?_
      decreases := ?_
      atomic := ?_
    }, ?_, ⟨s, by simp only [hs, if_true]⟩⟩
    · intro x hx
      simp only [hx, if_true]
    · intro x hx
      simp only [hx, if_false, hs, if_true]
      norm_num
    · intro x hx
      by_contra hnot
      simp only [hnot, if_false] at hx
      exact absurd hx (by norm_num)
    · intro x
      rfl

name: poly_gap_is_not_a_gap
stmt:
theorem poly_gap_is_not_a_gap (Sat : α → Prop) :
    (∃ R : Repair α, (∀ x, R.Sat x ↔ Sat x) ∧ ∃ x, R.μ x = 0) ↔ (∃ x, Sat x)
proof:
repair_iff_satisfiable Sat

end PolyRepair

end Lattice.Geo

name: affineExpr_eval
doc: **求值形式**：`(coord p axis + c)` 在 `pts` 上求值为 `pts p axis + c`。
stmt:
theorem affineExpr_eval (p : ℕ) (axis : Fin n) (c : ℝ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (affineExpr p axis c).evalPts pts = pts p axis + c
proof:
by
  unfold affineExpr
  simp [GeoExpr.evalPts]

name: affineZeroFix_reaches
doc:
**一步满足**：修复后 `coord p axis + c = 0`。

这是 `eqZero` 约束的确切内容。
stmt:
theorem affineZeroFix_reaches (p : ℕ) (axis : Fin n) (c : ℝ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.eqZero (affineExpr p axis c))
      (affineZeroFix p axis c pts)
proof:
by
  show (affineExpr p axis c).evalPts (affineZeroFix p axis c pts) = 0
  rw [affineExpr_eval]
  unfold affineZeroFix
  simp only [if_true, Function.update_same]
  ring

name: affineLeFix_reaches
doc:
**一步满足**：修复后 `coord p axis + c ≤ 0`。

**这依赖 `le_refl`：边界值满足 `≤`。**
严格不等式（`ltZero`）做不到这一点——实数没有最小正数。
stmt:
theorem affineLeFix_reaches (p : ℕ) (axis : Fin n) (c : ℝ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.leZero (affineExpr p axis c))
      (affineLeFix p axis c pts)
proof:
by
  show (affineExpr p axis c).evalPts (affineLeFix p axis c pts) ≤ 0
  rw [affineExpr_eval]
  unfold affineLeFix affineZeroFix
  simp only [if_true, Function.update_same]
  ring_nf
  exact le_refl 0

name: poly_specific_repairs
doc:
**多项式组的双轨覆盖**：`eqZero` 与 `leZero` 都有**具体算子**（线性单变量情形），
而第 65 轮的 `repair_iff_satisfiable` 给出**存在性**的一般形式。

⇒ **12 个 `GeoConstraint` 构造子的覆盖现在是：**

| 分组 | 具体算子 | 存在性定理 |
|:--|:--:|:--:|
| `samePoint` | ✅ | — |
| `perpendicular` | ✅ | — |
| `rightAngle` | ✅（归约到 `perpendicular`） | — |
| `sqDistEq` | ✅ | — |
| `equalLength` | ✅ | — |
| `collinear` | ✅ | — |
| `parallel` | ✅（Skolem 化） | — |
| `midpoint` | ✅ | — |
| **`eqZero`** | ✅ **线性情形（本节）** | ✅ 一般情形（第 65 轮） |
| **`leZero`** | ✅ **线性情形（本节）** | ✅ |
| **`ltZero` / `gtZero`** | ✅ **本节（显式 ε）** | ✅ |
| `angle` / `equalAngle` | ❌ 超越 | — |

⇒ **第 199 轮补上严格不等式的两条后，只剩 ngle / equalAngle 与一般 eqZero。**
stmt:
theorem poly_specific_repairs (p : ℕ) (axis : Fin n) (c : ℝ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.eqZero (affineExpr p axis c)) (affineZeroFix p axis c pts) ∧
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.leZero (affineExpr p axis c)) (affineLeFix p axis c pts)
proof: ⟨affineZeroFix_reaches p axis c pts, affineLeFix_reaches p axis c pts⟩

name: affineLtFix_reaches
doc: **一步满足**：修复后 coord p axis + c = -ε < 0，即 ltZero 成立。
stmt:
theorem affineLtFix_reaches (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (p : ℕ) (axis : Fin n) (c : ℝ)
    (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.ltZero (affineExpr p axis c)) (affineLtFix ε p axis c pts)
proof:
by
  unfold GeoConstraint.Holds affineExpr affineLtFix
  simp [GeoExpr.evalPts]
  linarith

name: affineGtFix_reaches
doc: **一步满足**：修复后 coord p axis + c = ε > 0，即 gtZero 成立。
stmt:
theorem affineGtFix_reaches (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (p : ℕ) (axis : Fin n) (c : ℝ)
    (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.gtZero (affineExpr p axis c)) (affineGtFix ε p axis c pts)
proof:
by
  unfold GeoConstraint.Holds affineExpr affineGtFix
  simp [GeoExpr.evalPts]
  linarith

name: poly_strict_repairs
doc: **两条严格修复同时成立**：ε > 0 时 ltZero 与 gtZero 都能一步到达。
stmt:
theorem poly_strict_repairs (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (p : ℕ) (axis : Fin n) (c : ℝ)
    (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.ltZero (affineExpr p axis c)) (affineLtFix ε p axis c pts) ∧
    GeoConstraint.Holds (.gtZero (affineExpr p axis c)) (affineGtFix ε p axis c pts)
proof:
⟨affineLtFix_reaches ε hε p axis c pts, affineGtFix_reaches ε hε p axis c pts⟩

end PolySpecificRepair

name: copy_preserves_at_sat
doc:
**The abstract layering applies to the geometric repair.**

At a satisfying state `samePointRepair` does not move, so it preserves every predicate whatsoever. This is
`Lattice.Core.Invariant.preserves_of_sat` instantiated, and it is the shared half of the quality scale: the
conservative layer is a theorem, not a convention.
stmt:
theorem copy_preserves_at_sat (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : (samePointRepair a b).Sat pts) (P : (ℕ → Pt n) → Prop) :
    P pts → P ((samePointRepair a b).fix pts)
proof: preserves_of_sat (samePointRepair a b) P pts h

name: project_preserves_at_sat
doc: **The same instantiation at the projecting repair**, whose step is a rotation rather than a copy.
stmt:
theorem project_preserves_at_sat (a b c e : ℕ) (hab : a ≠ b) (hcb : c ≠ b) (heb : e ≠ b)
    (hv : ∀ pts : ℕ → Pt n, (∑ j, (pts e j - pts c j) * (pts e j - pts c j)) ≠ 0)
    (pts : ℕ → Pt n) (h : (perpRepair a b c e hab hcb heb hv).Sat pts)
    (P : (ℕ → Pt n) → Prop) :
    P pts → P ((perpRepair a b c e hab hcb heb hv).fix pts)
proof:
preserves_of_sat (perpRepair a b c e hab hcb heb hv) P pts h

end Lattice.Geo

namespace Lattice.Lib.Linear

open Lattice.Core

name: linear_repair_preserves_at_sat
doc:
**The abstract layering also applies to the linear repair.**

`linearRepair` is the linear side's inhabitant of `Repair`; at a satisfying state it preserves every
predicate. Together with the two geometric instances above, this shows the layering is not an artefact of the
geometry module -- which was the reason for moving it into the core.
stmt:
theorem linear_repair_preserves_at_sat (a b : ℚ) (ha : a ≠ 0) (x : ℚ)
    (h : (linearRepair a b ha).Sat x) (P : ℚ → Prop) :
    P x → P ((linearRepair a b ha).fix x)
proof:
preserves_of_sat (linearRepair a b ha) P x h

end Lattice.Lib.Linear

name: encExpr_ge_two
doc: 每个编码至少两个 token（一个标签 + 至少一个操作数）。
stmt: theorem encExpr_ge_two (e : GeoExpr n) : 2 ≤ (encExpr e).length
proof:
by
  rw [encExpr_length]
  induction e with
  | coord p axis => show 2 ≤ 3; omega
  | const c => show 2 ≤ 2; exact Nat.le_refl 2
  | add a b iha ihb => show 2 ≤ 1 + encLenE a + encLenE b; omega
  | sub a b iha ihb => show 2 ≤ 1 + encLenE a + encLenE b; omega
  | mul a b iha ihb => show 2 ≤ 1 + encLenE a + encLenE b; omega

name: decExpr_coord
doc: **坐标往返**：3 个 token，还原坐标。
stmt:
theorem decExpr_coord (p : ℕ) (axis : Fin n) (fuel : ℕ) :
    decExpr (n := n) (fuel + 1) (encExpr (n := n) (.coord p axis)) = some (.coord p axis, 3)
proof:
by
  show decExpr (n := n) (fuel + 1)
      (Sum.inl tCoord :: Sum.inl p :: Sum.inl axis.val :: []) = some (.coord p axis, 3)
  rw [decExpr]
  simp only [tCoord_eq]
  norm_num

name: decExpr_const
doc:
**常量往返**：2 个 token，**且实数值原样返回**。

这是 `ℕ` token 类型做不到的事，也是本节引入 `Sum.inr` 的理由。
stmt:
theorem decExpr_const (c : ℝ) (fuel : ℕ) :
    decExpr (n := n) (fuel + 2) (encExpr (n := n) (.const c)) = some (.const c, 2)
proof:
by
  show decExpr (n := n) (fuel + 2) (Sum.inl tConst :: Sum.inr c :: []) = some (.const c, 2)
  rw [show (fuel + 2) = (fuel + 1) + 1 from rfl]
  rw [decExpr]
  simp only [tConst_eq, tCoord_eq]
  norm_num

end EqTok

end Lattice.Geo

name: decExpr_add_step
doc: Equation lemma for the add branch, arbitrary second token.
stmt:
theorem decExpr_add_step (k : ℕ) (d : EqTok) (rest : List EqTok) :
    decExpr (n := n) (k + 1) (Sum.inl tAdd :: d :: rest) =
      (match decExpr (n := n) k (d :: rest) with
       | some (x, c₁) =>
           match decExpr (n := n) k ((d :: rest).drop c₁) with
           | some (y, c₂) => some (.add x y, 1 + c₁ + c₂)
           | none => none
       | none => none)
proof:
by
  rw [decExpr.eq_def]
  simp only [tAdd_eq, tSub_eq, tMul_eq, tCoord_eq, tConst_eq]
  norm_num
  rfl

name: decExpr_sub_step
doc: Equation lemma for the sub branch, arbitrary second token.
stmt:
theorem decExpr_sub_step (k : ℕ) (d : EqTok) (rest : List EqTok) :
    decExpr (n := n) (k + 1) (Sum.inl tSub :: d :: rest) =
      (match decExpr (n := n) k (d :: rest) with
       | some (x, c₁) =>
           match decExpr (n := n) k ((d :: rest).drop c₁) with
           | some (y, c₂) => some (.sub x y, 1 + c₁ + c₂)
           | none => none
       | none => none)
proof:
by
  rw [decExpr.eq_def]
  simp only [tAdd_eq, tSub_eq, tMul_eq, tCoord_eq, tConst_eq]
  norm_num
  rfl

name: decExpr_mul_step
doc: Equation lemma for the mul branch, arbitrary second token.
stmt:
theorem decExpr_mul_step (k : ℕ) (d : EqTok) (rest : List EqTok) :
    decExpr (n := n) (k + 1) (Sum.inl tMul :: d :: rest) =
      (match decExpr (n := n) k (d :: rest) with
       | some (x, c₁) =>
           match decExpr (n := n) k ((d :: rest).drop c₁) with
           | some (y, c₂) => some (.mul x y, 1 + c₁ + c₂)
           | none => none
       | none => none)
proof:
by
  rw [decExpr.eq_def]
  simp only [tAdd_eq, tSub_eq, tMul_eq, tCoord_eq, tConst_eq]
  norm_num
  rfl

name: encLenE_ge_two
doc: `encLenE e ≥ 2`.
stmt: theorem encLenE_ge_two (e : GeoExpr n) : 2 ≤ encLenE e
proof:
by
  induction e with
  | coord p axis => show 2 ≤ 3; omega
  | const c => show 2 ≤ 2; exact Nat.le_refl 2
  | add a b iha ihb => show 2 ≤ 1 + encLenE a + encLenE b; omega
  | sub a b iha ihb => show 2 ≤ 1 + encLenE a + encLenE b; omega
  | mul a b iha ihb => show 2 ≤ 1 + encLenE a + encLenE b; omega

name: drop_encExpr
doc: Dropping an encoding's length from `encExpr e ++ X` leaves `X`.
stmt:
theorem drop_encExpr (e : GeoExpr n) (X : List EqTok) :
    (encExpr e ++ X).drop (encLenE e) = X
proof:
by
  rw [← encExpr_length (n := n) e]
  simp

name: decExpr_enc_nil
doc: **Every `GeoExpr` round-trips** through the real-carrying token stream.
stmt:
theorem decExpr_enc_nil (e : GeoExpr n) :
    decExpr (n := n) (encLenE e) (encExpr e) = some (e, encLenE e)
proof:
by
  have h := decExpr_enc e [] (encLenE e) (Nat.le_refl _)
  rwa [List.append_nil] at h


end EqTokRoundtrip

end Lattice.Geo

name: reinject_loss_eq_zero
doc:
**再注入：修正之后重新编译，惩罚在修正点为零。**

给定 `samePoint a b` 约束与任意初始点列 `pts`：

1. 修正得到 `pts' := (samePointRepair a b).iterate 1 pts`；
2. 修正后满足该约束（`fixSamePoint_holds`）；
3. 该约束的残差在 `pts'` 处为零（`samePoint` 分支的 `poly` 就是 `sqDist a b`，
   而满足即 `pts' a = pts' b`，故 `sqDist = 0`）；
4. 于是**再编译**得到的损失 `loss (.samePoint a b) pts'` 为零。

第 4 步是本节与 `reinject_sound` 的区别：那里没有 `loss`。
stmt:
theorem reinject_loss_eq_zero (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    EqConstraint.loss (.samePoint a b) ((samePointRepair a b).iterate 1 pts) = 0
proof:
by
  apply loss_eq_zero_of_poly_eq_zero
                                                                               
  have hhold : GeoConstraint.Holds (.samePoint a b) ((samePointRepair a b).iterate 1 pts) :=
    reinject_sound a b pts
                                                               
  have hsame : ((samePointRepair a b).iterate 1 pts) a
      = ((samePointRepair a b).iterate 1 pts) b := by
    simpa [GeoConstraint.Holds] using hhold
                                                                                    
  show EqConstraint.poly (.samePoint a b) ((samePointRepair a b).iterate 1 pts) = 0
  unfold EqConstraint.poly
  rw [sqDist_eq_zero_iff]
  exact hsame

name: reinject_correct
doc:
**再注入的完整陈述：修正后，惩罚为零。**

这条定理把闭环的三段串成一条：修正（`iterate 1`）→ 满足（隐含）→ 再编译（`loss`）为零。
`a`、`b` 与初始配置任意，所以它对**每一个**初始状态成立。
stmt:
theorem reinject_correct (a b : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    (GeoConstraint.Holds (.samePoint a b) ((samePointRepair a b).iterate 1 pts))
      ∧ EqConstraint.loss (.samePoint a b) ((samePointRepair a b).iterate 1 pts) = 0
proof:
⟨reinject_sound a b pts, reinject_loss_eq_zero a b pts⟩

end Reinjection

end Lattice.Geo

name: reinject_generic
doc:
**通用再注入**：只要「满足 `c` ⟹ `poly c` 为零」，损失就为零。

这条**不**假设 `c` 是哪个构造子。每新增一个约束，只需提供那条蕴含，
不必重做再注入的论证。
stmt:
theorem reinject_generic {n : ℕ} (c : EqConstraint n) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : EqConstraint.poly c pts = 0) :
    EqConstraint.loss c pts = 0
proof: Reinjection.loss_eq_zero_of_poly_eq_zero c pts h

name: reinject_of_hold
doc:
**形式更直接的版本**：把「满足 ⟹ 残差为零」作为参数。

`hhold : 满足 c 的点残差为零`，则修正到满足点后损失为零。
stmt:
theorem reinject_of_hold {n : ℕ} (c : EqConstraint n) (R : Repair (ℕ → Pt n))
    (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (hconv : R.Sat (R.iterate (R.μ pts) pts))
    (hhold : ∀ q, R.Sat q → EqConstraint.poly c q = 0) :
    EqConstraint.loss c (R.iterate (R.μ pts) pts) = 0
proof:
Reinjection.loss_eq_zero_of_poly_eq_zero c _
    (hhold _ hconv)

name: perpendicular_poly_eq_zero
doc:
**垂直性满足 ⟹ 残差为零**。

`poly (.perpendicular a b c e) pts` 按定义是 `∑ i, (pts b i - pts a i) * (pts e i - pts c i)`，
而 `Holds (.perpendicular ...)` 断言这个和为零。两者按定义一致。
stmt:
theorem perpendicular_poly_eq_zero {n : ℕ} (a b c e : ℕ) (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (h : GeoConstraint.Holds (.perpendicular a b c e) pts) :
    EqConstraint.poly (.perpendicular a b c e) pts = 0
proof:
by
  simpa [EqConstraint.poly, GeoConstraint.Holds] using h

name: reinject_perpendicular
doc:
**`perpendicular` 的再注入（通用形式）**：修正到满足点后，损失为零。

`hhold` 由调用方供给「该修复算子的满足点满足垂直性」。这样本定理对**任何**
修复算子成立，不必知道它内部把 `Sat` 写成什么形式——这正是参数化的意义。
stmt:
theorem reinject_perpendicular {n : ℕ} (a b c e : ℕ) (R : Repair (ℕ → Pt n))
    (pts : ℕ → Pt n)
    (hconv : R.Sat (R.iterate (R.μ pts) pts))
    (hhold : ∀ q, R.Sat q → GeoConstraint.Holds (.perpendicular a b c e) q) :
    EqConstraint.loss (.perpendicular a b c e) (R.iterate (R.μ pts) pts) = 0
proof:
reinject_of_hold (.perpendicular a b c e) R pts hconv
    (fun q hq => perpendicular_poly_eq_zero a b c e q (hhold q hq))

name: reinject_perpRepair
doc:
**`perpRepair` 的再注入**：修正到收敛点后，再编译的损失为零。

用 `iterate (μ pts)` 而非固定的 `1`，因为这与 `Repair.progress` /
`RepairConvergence.converges_within` 的口径一致：任何修复算子都保证
`Sat (iterate (μ x) x)`，而不一定是一步。

`hhold` 由 `perpRepair` 的定义直接给出：它的 `Sat` **就是**
`GeoConstraint.Holds (.perpendicular ...)`。
stmt:
theorem reinject_perpRepair {n : ℕ} (a b c e : ℕ) (hab : a ≠ b) (hcb : c ≠ b) (heb : e ≠ b)
    (hv : ∀ pts : ℕ → Pt n, (∑ j, (pts e j - pts c j) * (pts e j - pts c j)) ≠ 0)
    (pts : ℕ → Pt n) :
    EqConstraint.loss (.perpendicular a b c e)
      ((perpRepair a b c e hab hcb heb hv).iterate
        ((perpRepair a b c e hab hcb heb hv).μ pts) pts) = 0
proof:
reinject_perpendicular a b c e (perpRepair a b c e hab hcb heb hv) pts
    (Lattice.Core.RepairConvergence.converges_within _ pts)
    (fun q hq => hq)

end ReinjectionGeneral

end Lattice.Geo

name: no_identity_repair
doc:
**A repair operator cannot be the identity.**

If some point fails `Sat`, then no `Repair` instance has `fix = id`: the `decreases` law would demand
`μ x < μ x`.

This is the obstruction behind the failed trivial instance, stated so that it is not rediscovered by
experiment. It also explains why every instance in `Lattice.Lib.Linear` builds a move: the movement is
what `decreases` is about.
stmt:
theorem no_identity_repair (R : Lattice.Core.Repair α) (hfix : R.fix = fun x => x) :
    ∀ x : α, R.Sat x
proof:
by
  intro x
  by_contra h
  have hdec : R.μ (R.fix x) < R.μ x := R.decreases x h
  rw [hfix] at hdec
  exact lt_irrefl _ hdec

name: nonid_of_not_universal
doc:
**Consequently, a `Repair` whose target is not universal must move the state.**

The contrapositive of `no_identity_repair`, phrased as the call to action for a geometric instance: if
some configuration fails the constraint, whatever `fix` you supply has to change configurations.
stmt:
theorem nonid_of_not_universal (R : Lattice.Core.Repair α) (hnot : ∃ x : α, ¬ R.Sat x) :
    R.fix ≠ fun x => x
proof:
by
  intro hfix
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hnot
  exact hx (no_identity_repair R hfix x)

name: geo_repair_progress
doc:
**The progress guarantee transfers to any carrier**, geometry included.

`Repair.progress` is stated for an abstract `α`; this restates it at a geometric configuration type so
that a future instance can cite it without a type-class detour. It is the T4 statement, waiting for an
operator.
stmt:
theorem geo_repair_progress (R : Lattice.Core.Repair (ℕ → Pt n)) :
    ∀ pts : ℕ → Pt n, ∃ m : ℕ, R.Sat (R.iterate m pts)
proof:
fun pts => R.progress pts

end Lattice.Geo

name: iterate_fix_of_sat
doc:
**A satisfying state is a fixed point of every iterate.**

Immediate from `absorbs` by induction on the iterate: the state never changes, so it stays put.
stmt:
theorem iterate_fix_of_sat (R : Repair α) (x : α) (h : R.Sat x) :
    ∀ n : ℕ, R.fix^[n] x = x
proof:
by
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ k ih => rw [Function.iterate_succ_apply', ih, R.absorbs x h]
